newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BT, DPB seen creating strong NZ finance powerhouse.
newsitem.headline: BT, DPB seen creating strong NZ finance powerhouse.

text.p: The marriage between Bankers Trust NZ and Doyle Paterson Brown (DPB) will create a formidable competitor in the New Zealand market, giving DPB access to BT's wide network and balance sheet, brokers said on Wednesday.

Doyle Paterson director Murray Doyle said the Wellington-based institutional brokerage, with a staff of 22, would essentially remain the same but the name would change to BT Securities Ltd in the next few months.
"The business is strong and solid here so there will be no changes in terms of either personnel or operating style," Doyle told Reuters.
Staff at DPB are mostly involved in either research or sales. Doyle said that the full takeover by BTNZ, a unit of Bankers Trust New York, would be effective July 1.
Doyle said he expected the BTNZ-DPB to emerge as a kind of wholesale one-stop shop.

"It will be unique in New Zealand in that in a wholesale operation you've got currencies, bonds and equities under one roof. If you look at the most of the other major players they just don't encompass all of those things -- they have areas of excellence in individual parts," he said.
BTNZ, a highly-profitable niche player in its own right, has long wanted to play an equities role in New Zealand.
BTNZ chief executive Rob Morrison said the acquisition of DPB's equity research and distribution skills was an important addition to BTNZ.

"An equity specialist like DPB supplements BTNZ's existing strengths which include wholesale treasury operations, wholesale and retail funds management and corporate finance," Morrison said in a statement.
DPB has had links with Brierley Investments (BIL), having been closely involved in BIL's raid on Wilson and Horton and BIL's acquisition of Air NZ "B" shares.
It has also been involved in Telecom and TranzRail placements. More recently DPB teamed up with its part owner, FR Partners, for the Restaurant Brands float.
DPB has about 10 percent of the local market and has consistently ranked highly in Euromoney industry surveys.
Its move to team up with BTNZ means it is effectively the last major institutional brokerage to pass into foreign hands, following a trend that started several years ago.
Tim Preston, managing director at brokers ANZ Securities, said the move looked like a positive for both parties.

"It gives BT an arm they haven't had here before and in the case of Doyles it gives them access to a balance sheet and a distribution network that will enhance and complement what they've currently got," Preston said.
"From an industry perspective, we are going to have a more aggressive competitor, so it will continue to keep pressure on participants within that sector," he said.
DPB had been successful in carving out an international niche which others had found difficult to replicate, he noted.

Don Turkington, principal at the independent brokerage Cavill White Securities, said the move was yet more evidence of the internationalisation of the domestic market. "So we've more and more giants in a sort of Lilliput land," he said.
But Turkington was unperturbed at the prospect of a stronger competitor in DPB.
"These international franchises tend to dominate the broking industry, but having said that there is always a role for independents and every market has its specialists," he said.
